solution.setup: Use the population least-squares slope formula.
solution.sanityCheck: Because Z positively affects Y and is positively correlated with X, omitting Z biases the X coefficient upward.

keyInsight: An omitted predictor contaminates a coefficient in proportion to its effect and correlation with the included predictor.
recognitionCues: A regression omits a correlated variable that also drives the outcome.
commonMistakes: Assuming the fitted slope remains the structural coefficient 2.

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with Two Sigma, Jump Trading.

title: The Missing Variable Bias
problem: The true model is Y=2X+3Z+ε, where ε is uncorrelated with X, Var(X)=1, and Cov(X,Z)=0.4. If you regress Y only on X with an intercept, what population slope do you obtain?
